01 · Subject Property

The Home at Lot 71

A 1982 ATL manufactured home in Terrace Park, a well-maintained 55+ community in Evans. Major mechanical systems have been updated. All appliances are included. The home is being sold as-is — cosmetics are ready for the buyer's personal touches. No repairs or renovations by the seller.

The 55+ restriction narrows the buyer pool compared to an unrestricted park, which is fully reflected in the comparable sales below. The goal is to price for a fast, clean transaction and avoid compounding $1,015/month in lot rent through extended market time.

06 · Pricing Analysis

What this home should sell for

✦ Supports Higher End of Range

✓Prior sale at $32,000 (July 2023) is the strongest anchor — same lot, same home, only 3 years ago.
✓Roof ~7 years old on a composition shingle is still in its serviceable life. Less buyer objection than an end-of-life roof.
✓Furnace, A/C, and water heater replaced ~5 years ago. Buyers don't need to budget for HVAC replacement near-term.
✓All appliances included — move-in ready without additional purchase required.
✓Terrace Park is described as a clean, well-managed community. Park quality is a meaningful factor for 55+ buyers.
✓Carport with enclosed storage shed — practical, valued features for this buyer profile.

⚠ Pressure Toward Lower End

▲1982 construction — 40+ years old. Buyers apply an age discount regardless of updates.
▲Selling as-is with no cosmetic updates. Buyers will mentally budget for paint, flooring, and fixtures.
▲$1,015/mo lot rent is the highest in this comp set. Every dollar of lot rent reduces affordability.
▲55+ restriction limits the qualified buyer pool. Longer expected time to find the right buyer vs. unrestricted parks.
▲Same-park direct competitor (Lot #34) is active at $33,900 with 15 days on market. Must offer better value.
▲Market has shifted slightly since 2023. Rates and economic uncertainty have softened manufactured home demand.
Broker Recommendation
$28,000 – $33,000

Based on the sold comparables, active competition, and the seller's priority of a quick, low-friction sale, the recommended listing range is $28,000–$33,000. The sweet spot is around $31,500–$32,500 — just below the same-park competitor at $33,900, acknowledging three years of depreciation from the $32K sale, and positioned as the best-value home in Terrace Park.

At this price, the expectation is an offer within 2–3 weeks. If no offer in 21 days, a $1,500 reduction puts us at ~$30,000 — still well within the comp range, and cheaper than another month of $1,015 lot rent.

Cash-only strategy: Chattel financing exists for manufactured homes but is uncommon for 1982-vintage units in land-lease parks. Market this to cash buyers — often 55+ individuals with proceeds from a prior home sale.

07 · On-Site Discussion Points

Walk-through agenda

Items to cover during the on-site visit before any listing agreement is signed.

01

Verify Current Condition

Walk the home against the 2023 photos. Note any changes — positive or negative — that should be factored into final pricing or disclosed. Confirm appliances are still present and functional.

02

Resolve the Title — Chris Williams

Title is held JTWROS with Chris Williams. Identify who Chris is, their current status, and whether they can sign. If Marjory has passed, gather the death certificate before listing. This is the critical path item.

03

Confirm Lot Rent & Park Rules

Verify the current lot rent is $1,015/mo with Terrace Park management. Obtain the park's buyer application, income requirements, and age verification process so it's ready to hand to the first interested buyer.

04

Agree on Inclusions / Exclusions

Appliances are listed as included per the prior sale. Confirm which items will convey. The kitchen island was excluded in 2023 — clarify its status. Any furnishings the seller wants to negotiate separately should be identified now.

05

Finalize List Price & Sign

Review this CMA together, agree on the list price within the $28K–$33K range, and execute the listing agreement digitally before leaving the site — no Denver trip required.

06

21-Day Price Review Built In

Agree today on a predetermined price reduction trigger — if no offer in 21 days, reduce by $1,500. Setting this expectation upfront avoids difficult conversations later and keeps the carrying-cost math working for the seller.
